quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #17
										  					
  

20 Questions • Passing Score 14

questions.question: What does a broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line mean?

options.text: You can pass from the lane with the solid yellow line.
You cannot pass from either direction.
You can pass from the lane with the broken yellow line.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can pass from the lane with the broken yellow line.
questions.explanation: A broken yellow line means you can cross it to pass. A solid yellow line means you cannot pass. When they are together, only the side with the broken line allows passing.

questions.question: What shape is a stop sign?

options.text: Rectangle.
Square.
Circle.
Octagon.

questions.correctAnswerText: Octagon.
questions.explanation: Stop signs are eight-sided (octagon). This shape is used only for stop signs to tell drivers to come to a complete stop.

questions.question: What does a "No Parking" sign mean?

options.text: You cannot stop your vehicle there at all.
You can stop briefly to pick up or drop off passengers.
You can park there if the driver stays in the vehicle.
You can leave your vehicle for less than five minutes.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can stop briefly to pick up or drop off passengers.
questions.explanation: A "No Parking" sign allows you to stop temporarily to load or unload passengers or cargo. You cannot leave your vehicle unattended.

questions.question: If you are in an accident, what should you do?

options.text: Stop immediately.
Help the injured.
Call the police.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Stop right away. Move your vehicle out of traffic if possible. Call police and ask for an ambulance if needed. Help stop severe bleeding if you can. Wait for emergency responders to arrive.

questions.question: What does an orange-colored sign mean?

options.text: A no passing zone is starting.
A railroad crossing is ahead.
A school zone is ahead.
Construction work is ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Construction work is ahead.
questions.explanation: Orange signs warn of construction, maintenance, or emergency work. They have black symbols or text.

questions.question: What do yellow lines separate?

options.text: Traffic lanes on one-way streets.
Traffic moving in opposite directions on two-way roads.
All carpool lanes from regular traffic lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic moving in opposite directions on two-way roads.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines mark the center of roads used for two-way traffic. A solid yellow line means do not cross. A broken yellow line means you can cross to pass if it is safe.

questions.question: When changing lanes, you should never:

options.text: Change lanes inside an intersection.
Check your blind spot by looking over your shoulder.
Check for other drivers moving into the same lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes inside an intersection.
questions.explanation: Never change lanes inside an intersection. Always look over your shoulder to check your blind spot before changing lanes. Watch for other drivers who may be moving into the same lane.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Road construction ahead.
The road curves left then right.
The road curves right then left.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road curves right then left.
questions.explanation: This yellow warning sign tells you the road will curve right, then curve left. Slow down and be ready for these curves.

questions.question: Which is a strategy of defensive driving?

options.text: Looking straight ahead only.
Staying alert and keeping your eyes moving.
Expecting other drivers to fix your mistakes.
Being sure you can avoid danger at the last second.

questions.correctAnswerText: Staying alert and keeping your eyes moving.
questions.explanation: Keep scanning the road ahead and to the sides. Check your mirrors every few seconds. Traffic changes constantly, so you must stay alert and aware of everything around you.

questions.question: When you see a school crossing sign, you should:

options.text: Always stop, even without a stop sign.
Watch for children and be ready to stop.
Always honk your horn when you see children.
Be ready to help children cross the street.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch for children and be ready to stop.
questions.explanation: Always be ready to stop for pedestrians in crosswalks. Watch carefully for children at school crossings and be prepared to stop immediately.

questions.question: If you are driving on a highway next to a single broken white line, what can you do?

options.text: You cannot cross the line to pass.
You can cross the line to pass and change lanes.
You can only cross the line to change lanes if you are in the left lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can cross the line to pass and change lanes.
questions.explanation: Broken white lines separate lanes moving in the same direction. You can cross a broken white line to pass or change lanes if it is safe.

questions.question: When driving behind another vehicle at night, what should you do?

options.text: Keep your headlights on low beam.
Use high beams until you are within 10 feet of the vehicle ahead.
Use high beam headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your headlights on low beam.
questions.explanation: Use high beams only in rural areas when no other cars are nearby. Switch to low beams when following another vehicle closely.

questions.question: When a school bus stops to pick up or drop off children, what must you do?

options.text: Stop completely until all children have left the bus.
Stop completely until the red lights stop flashing and the stop arm is pulled back.
Change lanes and pass slowly and carefully.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely until the red lights stop flashing and the stop arm is pulled back.
questions.explanation: Stop when a school bus has flashing red lights and its stop arm extended. Wait until the lights stop flashing and the arm is pulled back. Even after the bus moves, do not go until you are sure no children are crossing the road.

questions.question: If you are about to be hit from behind, which should you NOT do?

options.text: Apply your brakes.
Let go of the steering wheel.
Press your head against the head restraint.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let go of the steering wheel.
questions.explanation: If hit from behind, your body will be thrown backward. Press yourself against your seat and put your head against the head restraint to prevent injury. Keep a firm grip on the steering wheel and be ready to brake.

questions.question: You must stop for a school bus in which situation?

options.text: When it is parked on the shoulder with no one in it.
When it approaches you, even if its lights are not flashing.
When you are both on a two-lane highway and its red lights are flashing.
Whenever the driver waves at you.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you are both on a two-lane highway and its red lights are flashing.
questions.explanation: Stop when approaching a school bus with flashing red lights that is picking up or dropping off children. On a two-lane road, traffic in both directions must stop and stay stopped while the red lights flash and the stop arm is extended.

questions.question: When can you drive across a broken white line?

options.text: At any time.
Only during daylight hours.
When it is safe to change lanes.
Only when passing a motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: When it is safe to change lanes.
questions.explanation: Broken white lines separate lanes moving in the same direction. You can cross broken lines to pass or change lanes if it is safe.

questions.question: When driving in rain, what lights should you use?

options.text: Low beam headlights.
High beam headlights.
Parking lights.
No lights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: In rain, use your low beam headlights.

questions.question: If you need to pass behind a large truck that is backing up, what should you do?

options.text: Pass quickly.
Wait for the truck to finish backing up before you pass.
Honk to alert the driver that you are passing.
Assume the driver can see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait for the truck to finish backing up before you pass.
questions.explanation: Large trucks have large blind spots behind them. The driver likely cannot see you. Always wait for the truck to finish backing up before you pass it.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Pedestrians ahead.
End of construction zone.
School crossing ahead.
Flagger ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Flagger ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that a flagger is ahead controlling traffic in a construction area.

questions.question: Many crashes happen because of:

options.text: Drivers going too fast for the conditions.
Drivers checking mirrors and blind spots regularly.
Drivers yielding the right-of-way.
Drivers keeping a four-second following distance.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers going too fast for the conditions.
questions.explanation: Many crashes are caused by drivers going too fast for conditions. Always drive within speed limits and slow down when conditions are poor.
